title.narrative: NIHR Development Awards Call 1: Tackling childhood obesity in Latin America and South Asia

description.narrative:
A low- and middle-income country (LMIC) award led by the Universidad Autónoma de Querétaro, Mexico that aims to tackle childhood obesity in Bangladesh, Mexico, and Pakistan.
In Bangladesh, Mexico, and Pakistan, overweight and obesity is common among children, posing serious risks to their health. Childhood obesity persists into adulthood and increases the likelihood of chronic diseases, including heart disease, diabetes, cancer, and mental health problems. The impact extends beyond individual health, straining healthcare resources and hindering economic growth.
Previous attempts to address childhood obesity have had limited success, underscoring the need for innovative and culturally sensitive approaches. These should address both individual and environmental factors and should be tailored to the specific contexts of these countries.
Commencing in January 2025, the twelve-month award involves the assembly of researchers, community representatives, and policymakers from the three countries to develop a research proposal aimed at tackling the epidemic of childhood obesity. Planned activities include a review of the latest research on the topic, training individuals in developing high-quality research proposals, consulting stakeholders, and defining important outcomes. Activities will be conducted through a combination of in-person and online engagements to maximise efficiency and inclusivity. The primary output of this award is the development of a research funding proposal to tackle the issue of childhood obesity.
The proposed research will fill critical knowledge gaps regarding prevention and management of childhood obesity. By involving children, parents, and teachers in the design process, the award will work to develop interventions that address various contributing factors, including diet, physical activity, sleep, and environmental influences.

The award has four objectives:
1. To strengthen the applicant team by identifying and inviting additional experts, policymakers, and representatives of relevant community organisations to participate in our research.
2. To build capacity to develop, submit and manage global health research awards and to engage communities in research.
3. To develop the future research programme by searching for the most important information gaps, refining research questions, identifying outcomes that are important to stakeholders, and writing the research funding application.
4. To establish equitable South-South and North-South partnership by agreeing shared values, equitable distribution of responsibilities, determining a transparent decision-making process, and achieving gender equity.
